arxiv-2303-09049.title: On the 3D Curvature and Dynamics of the Musca filament Facilities: SOFIA (HAWC+), APEX, ALMA, Planck, Herschel astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ; Astropy Collaboration et al. 2018 )
arxiv-2303-09049.creator: Aidan Kaminsky, Lars Bonne, Doris Arzoumanian, Simon Coudé
arxiv-2303-09049.description: Abstract Filaments are ubiquitous in the interstellar medium (ISM), yet their formation and evolution remains the topic of intense debate. In order to obtain a more comprehensive view of the 3D morphology and evolution of the Musca filament, we model the C 18 O(2-1) emission along the filament crest with several large-scale velocity field structures.

arxiv-2308-06692.title: SimMatchV2: Semi-Supervised Learning with Graph Consistency
arxiv-2308-06692.creator: Mingkai Zheng, Shan You, Lang Huang, Chen Luo, Fei Wang, Chen Qian, Chang Xu
arxiv-2308-06692.description: Abstract Semi-Supervised image classification is one of the most fundamental problem in computer vision, which significantly reduces the need for human labor. In this paper, we introduce a new semi-supervised learning algorithm - SimMatchV2, which formulates various consistency regularizations between labeled and unlabeled data from the graph perspective.

arxiv-2310-05830.title: Radio pulsars resonantly accelerating electrons
arxiv-2310-05830.creator: Zaza N. Osmanov, Swadesh M. Mahajan
arxiv-2310-05830.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Zaza N. Osmanov, Swadesh M. Mahajan. Based on the recently demonstrated resonant wave-wave process, it is shown that electrons can be accelerated to ultra-relativistic energies in the magnetospheres of radio pulsars. The energization occurs via the resonant interaction of the electron wave (described by a Klein-Gordon (KG) equation) moving in unison with an intense electromagnetic (EM) wave; the KG wave/particle continuously draws energy from EM.

arxiv-2409-15979.title: Finetuning LLMs for Comparative Assessment Tasks
arxiv-2409-15979.creator: Vatsal Raina, Adian Liusie, Mark Gales
arxiv-2409-15979.description: Abstract Automated assessment in natural language generation is a challenging task. Instruction-tuned large language models (LLMs) have shown promise in reference-free evaluation, particularly through comparative assessment. However, the quadratic computational complexity of pairwise comparisons limits its scalability. To address this, efficient comparative assessment has been explored by applying comparative strategies on zero-shot LLM probabilities.

arxiv-2410-12910.title: Effects of threshold resummation for large- x x PDF in large momentum effective theory
arxiv-2410-12910.creator: Xiangdong Ji, Yizhuang Liu, Yushan Su, Rui Zhang
arxiv-2410-12910.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Xiangdong Ji, Yizhuang Liu, Yushan Su, Rui Zhang. Parton distribution functions (PDFs) at large x x are challenging to extract from experimental data, yet they are essential for understanding hadron structure and searching for new physics beyond the Standard Model.

arxiv-2504-20931.title: Generalized Cluster Algebras are Subquotients of Cluster Algebras
arxiv-2504-20931.creator: Rolando Ramos David Whiting
arxiv-2504-20931.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Rolando Ramos David Whiting. Generalized Cluster Algebras (GCA) are generalizations of Cluster Algebras (CA) with higher-order exchange relations. Previously, Chekhov-Shapiro conjectured that every GCA can be embedded into a CA. In this paper, we prove a modified version of this conjecture by providing a construction that realizes a given GCA as subquotient of some CA, as an algebra over the ground ring of the GCA via restriction of scalars.

pmc-10648761.description: According to Resolution 235 adopted during the World Radiocommunication Conference 2015 (WRC-15) and the preliminary agenda item 1.5 of WRC-2023, the International Telecommunication Union Radiocommunication Sector (ITU-R) has been entrusted to carry out sharing and compatibility studies between broadcasting and mobile services in the frequency range 470–694 MHz in Region 1.

pmc-10675066.title: Development of New Hybrid Composites for High-Temperature Applications
pmc-10675066.creator: Rubén Seoane-Rivero, Lorena Germán, Fernando Santos, Koldo Gondra, Florian Puch, Bodo Fiedler
pmc-10675066.description: Nowadays, in the automation and aircraft industries, there is a challenge in minimizing the weight of components of vehicles without losing the original properties. In this study, we fabricate hybrid composites based on fiber metal laminates; these materials could be promising composites for high-performance applications.

pmc-11473724.title: Increasing handgrip strength via post-hypnotic suggestions with lasting effects
pmc-11473724.creator: Ulrike Nieft, Marleen Schlütz, Barbara Schmidt
pmc-11473724.description: In our study, we suggested participants to feel strong during hypnosis and tested if that affected their handgrip strength. Handgrip strength is measured via a hand dynamometer and indicates muscle strength and participants’ general medical condition. In addition, we obtained subjective ratings of strength via a visual analogue scale.

pmc-11579596.title: CPR training as a gender and rights-based healthcare issue
pmc-11579596.creator: Rebecca Amalia Szabo, Kirsty Forrest, Peter Morley, Stephanie Barwick, Komal Bajaj, Kellie Britt, Sarah A Yong, Jocelyn Park-Ross, David Story, Jessica Stokes-Parish
pmc-11579596.description: It is not understood how cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training, specifically the representation of sex in CPR manikins, contributes to inequitable outcomes in cardiac arrest survival. The aim of this study was to identify the sex and chest wall secondary sexual characteristics of CPR manikins on the global market.

pmc-11603729.title: Novel polyomavirus in the endangered garden dormouse Eliomys quercinus
pmc-11603729.creator: Emilija Vasiliūnaitė, Monika Repšytė, Eva Marie Kramer, Johannes Lang, Christine Jelinek, Rainer G Ulrich, Christopher B Buck, Alma Gedvilaitė
pmc-11603729.description: BackgroundThe garden dormouse (Eliomys quercinus) has experienced a significant population decline across Europe in recent decades. While habitat loss and climate change are often cited as primary factors, pathogen exposure, either to novel or to previously known, may play a role in such a decline.

pmc-11690130.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). PA Health & Wellness, a managed care organization in Pennsylvania, has collaborated with Johns Hopkins on deploying the academic Maximizing Independence at Home (“MIND at Home”) Program for community-living individuals with cognitive impairment who have Medicaid Long-Term Support Services. This home-based model is aimed at coordinating care and supporting caregivers for individuals who are cognitively complex and at risk for out of home placement.

pmc-12734235.title: Aspergillus Endocarditis in Native Valves in Non-Traditional Hosts: A Systematic Review of a Case in a Patient with CREST Syndrome and Advanced Liver Cirrhosis
pmc-12734235.creator: Leticia Espinosa-del-Barrio, Elia Gómez G de la Pedrosa, Noelia Álvarez-Díaz, Javier Guzmán Martínez, María Dolores Corbacho Loarte, Rosa Escudero Sánchez, Pilar Martín-Dávila, Jesús Fortún Abete, Javier Cobo Reinoso, Vicente Pintado García, Francesca Gioia, Ayman O Soubani
pmc-12734235.description: Background: Aspergillus endocarditis is a rare but life-threatening form of infective endocarditis that typically occurs in patients with a history of cardiac surgery, prosthetic valve implantation, or profound immunosuppression. Native valve involvement in non-traditional hosts remains exceptionally rare and is diagnostically challenging.

pmc-12739113.title: IFN-γ and IL-4 correlate with protection induced by an attenuated malaria vaccine
pmc-12739113.creator: Tanisha M. Robinson, Jessica S. Bolton, Elisabeth H. Duncan, Elke S. Bergmann-Leitner, Marie Mura
pmc-12739113.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Controlled human malaria infections after immunization via mosquito bites with radiation attenuated Plasmodium falciparum sporozoites are necessary tools to decipher immune signatures of malaria protection. The phenotype of circulating mononuclear innate cells and the PBMC response to in vitro stimulation unraveled correlates of protection from baseline immune response to sporozoite stimulation (IFN-ƴ secretion and HLA-DRhigh expression) to vaccine-induced immune factors (IL-4 secretion and CD57- γδ T cell frequency). Understanding correlates of protection of infectious diseases is key for vaccine development.
